en.title: Marvel's Extreme Measures to Guard Avengers: Doomsday Secrets Revealed
en.summary: Marvel Studios is deploying unprecedented spoiler prevention tactics for the highly anticipated **Avengers: Doomsday**, opting out of early screenings for major awards bodies. This move signals a new level of secrecy for the franchise's biggest event.
en.body:
The internet is abuzz with speculation, and the final trailer for **Avengers: Doomsday** has only intensified the fervor. Teasing moments like **Cyclops** finally embodying his heroic potential, **Steve Rogers** finding a semblance of peace, and a monumental clash involving the **Avengers**, **X-Men**, and **Fantastic Four** against reanimated **Sentinels**, the film is poised to be a colossal hit. To ensure that anticipation translates into maximum impact, Marvel Studios is employing a spoiler prevention strategy that feels more like a fortress than a film release.

In a move that has raised eyebrows, Marvel and Disney have decided not to screen **Avengers: Doomsday** for awards voting committees, including prestigious bodies like the BAFTAs, Golden Globes, and Critics Choice Awards. This decision, reported by Variety, is a clear attempt to keep the film's narrative surprises under wraps until its December 18, 2026, release. While ticket sales are already projected to be massive and trailers have generated considerable discussion, this level of secrecy goes beyond typical industry practices. It echoes past efforts, such as when only key actors received full scripts for **Avengers: Infinity War**, or when a pivotal funeral scene in **Avengers: Endgame** was mislabeled as a "wedding" to throw off potential leaks.

## A History of Keeping Secrets

Marvel's commitment to guarding its cinematic universe's secrets is not new. For **Avengers: Endgame**, the studio went to extraordinary lengths, even using misleading footage in trailers. Similarly, **Avengers: Infinity War**'s promotional material featured scenes that ultimately didn't make it into the final cut. This pattern suggests a deliberate, long-standing approach to managing audience expectations and preserving the shock value of their most significant releases. The extensive measures for **Avengers: Doomsday** appear to be an escalation of this established protocol, indicating that the stakes for this particular film are exceptionally high.

## The Fan Frenzy and What It Means

For the passionate global fanbase of **WeCult**, this extreme secrecy is both frustrating and exhilarating. It fuels online discussions, encourages theories, and heightens the collective desire to experience the film unspoiled. While some might see it as excessive, it underscores the immense cultural weight **Avengers: Doomsday** is expected to carry. The decision to delay the film's release, which also impacted its IMAX screen availability due to a conflict with **Dune: Part 3**, further emphasizes Marvel's commitment to ensuring this cinematic event lands with maximum force. This isn't just about ticket sales; it's about controlling the narrative and delivering a viewing experience that resonates deeply with fans who have followed these characters for years.

What's Next

With **Avengers: Doomsday** set to premiere on December 18, 2026, fans will have to rely on the carefully curated trailers and official announcements for clues. The studio's commitment to secrecy suggests that the biggest reveals are being saved for the big screen.

content_raw: The hype for Avengers: Doomsday has hit a fever pitch, thanks to the release of its final trailer . X-Men fans got to see James Marsden finally embody everything that makes Cyclops great . The emotional moments showing Steve Rogers starting a family would melt even the hardest of hearts. And the money shot of Avengers, X-Men, and Fantastic Four battling against a legion of reanimated Sentinels is pure comic booky goodness. It’s all but guaranteed that Doomsday is going to be the biggest movie of the year, and Marvel Studios is taking every precaution to make sure it stays that way. A report from Variety notes that Marvel and Disney are choosing not to screen Doomsday for awards voting committees, including the BAFTAs, the Golden Globes, and the Critics Choice Awards. This move is more than likely to prevent spoilers ahead of the movie’s debut, yet it feels like an extreme measure. After all, ticket sales have been massive, and each subsequent trailer has sparked discussion. People are going to see this movie no matter what. It’s not the first time Marvel Studios has gone to extreme lengths to keep surprises secret. When Avengers: Infinity War was filming, only Chris Evans and Robert Downey Jr. were given the complete script; the rest of the cast received solely their respective scenes. Things were taken to an extreme level for Avengers: Endgame , as the scene where nearly the entire Marvel Cinematic Universe gathers for Tony Stark’s funeral was labeled a “wedding.” Further keeping spoilers close to the chest, Endgame ’s trailers only featured select footage from its opening act while Infinity War ’s trailer featured scenes that weren’t even in the movie. Doomsday has kept its trailers similarly lowkey. Apart from showcasing Doom as a major threat and hinting that the fate of the universe is at stake, nothing’s been said about how the Avengers come together or what draws them into the path of the X-Men and the Fantastic Four. That’s mystery enough, meaning that Marvel and Disney should be able to screen Doomsday for awards bodies without major twists getting leaked. Speaking as a film critic, I can tell you that early viewers of major films are given a list of requested “do not reveals” before a screening, and shape their coverage accordingly.  Most comic fans also know that Doomsday is drawing from one major comic book arc: the “Time Runs Out” storyline that ran through Jonathan Hickman’s Avengers and New Avengers . “Time Runs Out” lives up to its name and then some, as the Avengers and the Illuminati race to stop a series of world-ending incursions from shattering all of reality. Previous MCU movies, particularly Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness , have set up elements from “Time Runs Out” including the incursions and the multiverse, so anyone who’s read those comics has an inkling of what to expect once Doomsday hits the big screen.
